residency.test: Resident if you have your domicile (a home you keep and use) or habitual abode of more than six months in Luxembourg.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes for residents. Cross-border workers from Belgium, France and Germany are taxed on Luxembourg employment income and can often elect to be treated as residents.
residency.impatriate_regime: A regime for inbound employees exempts 50% of gross annual remuneration up to 400,000, replacing the older cost-reimbursement approach.

headline.rates: 0% to 42% across 23 brackets, plus an employment fund surcharge of 7% or 9%
headline.tax_classes: class 1 for single taxpayers, class 1a for single parents and over-64s, class 2 for jointly taxed couples
headline.capital_gains: speculative gains taxed in full; long-held assets largely exempt

income_tax.name: Impôt sur le revenu
income_tax.note: simplified from the statutory 23-bracket scale for tax class 1; the real scale steps in 2% increments

married_joint.note: tax class 2 splits income between the spouses

surcharges.name: Contribution au fonds pour l'emploi
surcharges.note: 9% where taxable income exceeds roughly 150,000 (class 1) or 300,000 (class 2)

standard_deduction.name: Frais d'obtention forfaitaires
standard_deduction.note: flat employment expense allowance; commuting relief (frais de déplacement) is separate

employee.name: Assurance dépendance
employee.note: charged on income above a quarter of the minimum wage, with no ceiling

capital_gains.speculative: gains on assets held six months or less are taxed at ordinary progressive rates
capital_gains.long_held: gains on securities held more than six months are exempt unless you hold a substantial participation of more than 10%
capital_gains.real_estate: gains on property held more than two years are taxed at half the global rate, with an allowance; your main home is exempt
capital_gains.note: the six-month rule makes Luxembourg unusually attractive for medium-term investors

quirks: Tax class matters enormously. Non-resident cross-border workers, married couples with a non-resident spouse, and single parents each face different scales, and the class assigned on your tax card is not always the optimal one.
The employment fund surcharge adds 7% or 9% on top of the tax itself, so the real top marginal rate is about 45.8%.
Interest paid on a personal loan, life insurance premiums and private pension contributions are all deductible within limits - Luxembourg has more of these small deductions than most systems.
Cross-border commuters can request to be taxed as residents, which lets them deduct foreign mortgage interest and use class 2. Whether it helps depends on the spouse's income.
Securities held more than six months escape capital gains tax entirely, which is one of the most generous treatments in the EU.

reporting.who_must_file: Residents with income above 100,000, with multiple employers, with non-employment income above thresholds, or who want to claim deductions. Others may be settled by an annual payroll adjustment (décompte annuel).

warnings: The statutory scale has 23 brackets stepping in 2% increments; the schedule here is a close but simplified reproduction.
Tax class 1a is not modelled - single parents and taxpayers over 64 pay less than the class 1 figures shown.
The 9% employment fund surcharge for high incomes is not switched on automatically.
